rationale: itnet_v2-claude-agentic: itnet_k=1, unet_c=64, itnet_alpha_init=0.0026, residual_learning=False, pretrain_lr=0.00025, pretrain_epochs=15, pretrain_patience=15, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=1200, val_n=200, seed=42, rationale=ITER-8 (breast itnet_v2, extend-to-20, 20-min budget). SIX-BOX (VERIFIED): i5 c32/n1200 hr0.8499; i6 c32/n2400 hr0.8574 (~15min, near budget); i7 c48/n1200 hr0.8621 (BEST, beats i6 at HALF the data, well within budget). (2) FINDING: denoiser WIDTH is the EFFICIENT lever -- c32->c48 at n1200 gave +0.012 (bigger than data doubling's +0.0075) and stays in budget, while data-scaling is diminishing AND expensive. (3) ONE KNOB: unet_c 48 -> 64. Hold n=1200 (fast, in-budget), k=1 (locked), all else = champion (alpha0.0026, residual False, lr2.5e-4, epochs15, patience15, grad_clip1.0, val_n200, seed42). (4) HYPOTHESIS: if c 48->64, hr rises above 0.8621 because the capacity axis is still paying (c16->32 +0.009, c32->48 +0.012 -- not yet saturated) and the wider denoiser closes more of the val generalization gap. FALSIFIER: hr <= ~0.863 (flat/down) => width saturates at 48; iter-9 pivots to DEPTH (more U-Net levels via a different knob) or combines best-c with n2400, or tunes pretrain_epochs. (5) BUDGET: c64/n1200 ~1.8x c48 conv FLOPs on the fast n1200 base (i7 fit comfortably) -> well under 20min. (6) Serial gated loop; dispatch iter-9 only after iter-8 writes numeric-hr observation.json.
